subject: Procurement onboarding checkpoint — renewal + capacity increase
messages:

Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2026-11-28T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal intake — procurement portal + onboarding for expansion

Hi Laura / Grace,

Thanks for the quick chats this week. Acme is ready to move forward with the renewal and the requested capacity increase for Q1. Procurement has asked us to submit the updated onboarding bundle through our portal so their systems can kick-off PO issuance and internal approvals.

Attached: Acme_Procurement_Form.pdf (fillable) — please complete the vendor details and the updated pricing line items so procurement can map to the correct cost center. Also attaching the portal link below for the intake form.

Portal link: https://acme.procure.example/portal/req/8492

High level ask from Acme procurement:
- Confirm new committed capacity (increase from 250k tokens/mo to 500k tokens/mo)
- Confirm term (they prefer 12 -> 18 months if possible)
- Provide a copy of the quote and SOW redline for legal review

Can you return the completed form by Tuesday EOD (Nov 30)? Procurement says that once the portal intake is complete they will route to finance and the PO should be generated within 3 business days.

Best,
Jane
Jane Doe
Head of Procurement — Acme Media

Attachment: Acme_Procurement_Form.pdf (application/pdf, 196KB)

Subject: Re: Renewal intake — procurement portal + onboarding for expansion

Jane — thanks, got it. Looping in Ben and Monica to own the quote and procurement fields. A few quick notes so we’re aligned:

- Capacity: we can commit to 500k tokens/mo but want to confirm cadence for burst usage and whether Acme expects smoothing across months.
- Term: we can offer an 18-month term with a stepped pricing benefit at the 12 and 18-month marks (details to follow in the quote).
- PO path: Ben — can you prepare the intake fields and attach the updated quote? Monica — can you confirm billing codes and any required remittance instructions for the portal form?

Proposed next steps:
1) Ben creates updated quote + SOW redline and shares here (cc legal if needed)
2) I’ll complete the Acme portal form and submit once Ben confirms the line items
3) Jane confirms whether Acme wants a DocuSign PO after procurement issues the internal PO, or if they’ll export from the portal and we attach 

Thanks — will aim to get the form submitted by EOD Nov 30.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

On Nov 28, 2026, at 11:02, laura.bennett@redwood.com wrote:
> Jane — thanks, got it. Looping in Ben and Monica to own the quote and procurement fields.

Attached is the updated quote: RDW_Quote_Expansion_2026.xlsx. Summary below for the portal form:

- Line item A: Base committed capacity — 500,000 tokens/month — $0.0009/token (monthly billing)
- Line item B: Burst buffer (on-demand) — up to 20% above commitment — billed at $0.0012/token
- Term: 18 months (start 2027-01-01, end 2028-06-30)
- Early termination: standard pro-rata with 60-day notice
- SLA: 99.9% uptime on Dedicated, with documented fallbacks to Hosted during maintenance windows

Monica — billing info for the portal: Redwood tax ID 27-3948123; remittance: remittance@redwood.com; net-30 standard. If Acme requires a different invoice cadence we can support net-45 for enterprise procurement but need to flag to finance.

I’ve redlined the SOW (attached SOW_redline_v1.docx) with the capacity changes and a short paragraph describing the burst smoothing. Legal should be able to do a quick pass — scope changes are limited.

Thanks Ben — that looks straightforward. Two quick portal items procurement flagged that I want to confirm before they run the intake:

1) They need a single-line description for the vendor in the system (max 140 chars). Suggested: "Redwood Inference — LLM inference platform (dedicated & hosted)"
2) Procurement also requires the vendor's primary contact for remittance and a contact for technical onboarding.

We’ll proceed with the 18-month term and the 500k committed capacity. Procurement asked whether Redwood prefers the portal-generated PO or a signed DocuSign PO from our standard template. They typically accept portal POs but we prefer DocuSign for our records. If procurement is OK emitting their PO and then we counter-sign via DocuSign that works.

I’ve created a portal intake ticket here: https://acme.procure.example/portal/req/8492 — you should be able to see the fields after submission. Procurement aims to issue an internal PO within 72 business hours after intake if all fields are correct.

Happy to do a 15-min sync if you want to run through the portal fields before submission.

Best,
Jane
